summary:
I built all five favourites fixes in scripts/gameindex. 279 tests pass: the gameindex suites, 88 new tests in tests/python/test_patch_favourites.py, plus test_autodeploy, test_host_duties and test_unrealgold_server. Nothing is committed, deployed, written to the share or sent to a box.

1. Labels. `favorites.clean_label` removes control characters for every writer. The Q3/Q2 comment labels also turn ';' into a space and '"' into "'". A test uses a transcription of ioq3 1.36's Cbuf_Execute to prove every command the engine would run from our block is one seta/set line. The hostnames tried include ';', '"', CR/LF, NUL and DEL. An existing box line with an unsafe comment is never called "unchanged", so it gets rewritten.

2. Team Arena. New TITLES["missionpack"]: engine q3cache, accepts {missionpack}, and internet servers must report missionpack too (a TA client cannot join baseq3). It is derived from each ioquake3 row whose folder has missionpack\ beside it.
- `sync.push_servercache` finds %APPDATA% with REGREAD HKCU Shell Folders\AppData and writes <AppData>\Quake3\servercache.dat.
- It never creates a folder, is BUSY while any Q3 client runs, asks PROCLIST again just before the upload, reads the file back and reports FAILED on any mismatch. A file not in the 1.36 layout is refused.
- The layout is proven against the ioq3 source at the 1.36 release point (git 06954842) and by disassembling the staged ioquake3.x86.exe (md5 12f99bc0…). The binary's size check is 0xa9200, its arrays are 0xa4000 + 0x5200 bytes, the CL_SetServerInfo field offsets match, NA_IP is 4, and NET_CompareAdr compares only type, ip and port.
- Entries we add carry a 16-byte mark in netadr_t.ip6, which the engine never reads for IPv4. Only marked entries are ever removed. The global count, the 4096 global records and the player's own favourites are kept byte for byte.

3. BUSY per file. `sync.plan_targets` groups titles by target path, compared case-insensitively. A file is BUSY if the exe of any title that reads it is running, and the log gives one line per file naming the path and the keys (e.g. "ioquake3+quake3"). The PROCLIST match is now case-insensitive, so the guard can fire on Win98 (.243).

4. A settled box reports "unchanged".
- `favorites.same_favourites` treats a file as unchanged when the game would see the same servers and every other line is identical. Order, labels, whitespace and a lastplayed stamp CS wrote itself are ignored.
- Slots are stable: a kept server keeps its serverN/adrN slot, or its place in the list.
- Servers the box already lists stay while they are still eligible (`db.best_servers(incumbent=...)`); the ranking only fills gaps.
- Hand-picked seed servers are no longer collapsed to one per host, which ends the UT99 flip.
- Ping is timed to the first reply.
- The vdf "address" key gets one tab, as revSrvBrowser writes it, and a rewrite keeps the game's lastplayed stamp.
- An offline replay of every file captured from the boxes against a DB snapshot: the second pass says "unchanged" for all 43 files.

5. Skip reasons. Rewritten from verified facts: jka, descent3, tribes2, hl2, sof2, halflife. halflife now says protocol 45: the WON hw.dll compares with 45 (cmp eax,2Dh), so 46 was wrong. New reasons: bf1942, heretic, hexen, doom3, farcry. wolfmp (RTCW) and deusex had writers that reported success but no screen in either game reads them; both are now listed as not written, with the reason.

Also fixed, all found by the audits and all in scripts/gameindex:
- No MKDIR any more; an empty folder listing is checked one level up.
- A box mid-GAMESYNC is deferred.
- A box whose re-index failed is not written.
- A lost host address now fails the pass (ok:false).
- Files are read and written as latin-1, so bytes ≥0x80 survive.
- Q3/Q2 player counts are humans only (ping > 0).
launcher_changes_needed:
LIBRARY (staged configs, another agent; favourites code needs nothing staged): in staged Quake-engine autoexec.cfg files, remove every ';' that sits outside quotes in a '//' comment. id Q2 3.20 / Q3 1.32 / ioq3 1.36 Cbuf_Execute split the line there and run the rest as a command. Full list with line numbers: .claude/evidence-1080p/build-favourites/staged-autoexec-semicolons.txt. Replace ';' with ' -':
- Quake3-TeamArena/baseq3/autoexec.cfg and missionpack/autoexec.cfg, lines 4 ('...rewritten on exit; this is not.') and 16 ('...\screenshots\;').
- Quake2Complete/{baseq2,rogue,xatrix}/autoexec.cfg and Quake2Win9x/baseq2/autoexec.cfg, lines 15 ('has no +use; invuse is its action key' runs `invuse` at every start) and 28 ('always run; nobody wants...').
- JediAcademy/base/autoexec.cfg line 2; SoldierOfFortune/base/autoexec.cfg line 26; SoldierOfFortune2/base/autoexec.cfg line 36.
- SiNGold/{base,ctf,2015}/autoexec.cfg: several comment lines, including an awk one-liner with ';'.
Then run the purge + GAMESYNC fix loop on every box.

tests/README.md (shared index file; tests/python/test_readme_lists_every_test.py fails until a row exists; it already fails on master for test_sharewrite.py and every new test_patch_*.py). Add this row to the 'Fix -> test coverage' table: | **favourites agent 2026-09-29: a public hostname in a Q3/Q2 favourites comment could run console commands (Cbuf splits at ';' inside //); Team Arena favourites via ioquake3 1.36 servercache.dat (layout pinned to the staged binary); BUSY per FILE and case-insensitive (quake3+ioquake3 share one autoexec, Win98 PROCLIST is upper-case); a settled box says unchanged (incumbents, stable slots, semantic compare, seeds not deduped by host, first-reply RTT); no MKDIR above a title folder; RTCW/Deus Ex writers were false successes; stale UNWRITABLE reasons corrected** | `scripts/gameindex/{favorites,sync,db,masters}.py` | `python/test_patch_favourites.py` |

CLAUDE.md, 'One Staged Tree, Eight Monitors', id Tech 3 bullet: the parenthetical '(retro-gameindex writes one)' is false. No gameindex code has ever referenced APPDATA except the new Team Arena servercache.dat writer, and no box has that autoexec. Suggested wording: 'a per-user %APPDATA%\Quake3\baseq3\autoexec.cfg would SHADOW the staged file entirely (none exists on the fleet as of 2026-09-29; retro-gameindex writes the install tree's autoexec.cfg, plus %APPDATA%\Quake3\servercache.dat for Team Arena's favourites)'.

retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md (findings log; outside this builder's area), newest first. Three entries:
(a) Q2/Q3 Cbuf_Execute splits at ';' outside quotes even inside a // comment: comment text after ';' runs as a command.
(b) Team Arena's Favorites tab is the ENGINE's list in %APPDATA%\Quake3\servercache.dat, not server1..16. ioq3 1.36 layout: 12-byte header, size field 692736, 4096+128 records of 164 bytes, netadr_t 32 bytes with the port in network order. Proven from the source and the staged binary.
(c) The staged WON Half-Life is protocol 45 (hw.dll cmp eax,2Dh), not 46.

LIBRARY doc: JediAcademy/SERVERS-fleet.txt still says the client is blocked by 'Disk 1 not in drive'. README-FLEET.txt in the same tree records the disc-mount fix (2026-08-31) and a two-box join, so SERVERS-fleet.txt should be updated to match.

OPTIONAL, agent release (not needed by this change): GAMEINDEX signatures for FarCry.exe and DOOM3.exe. Their UNWRITABLE answers already exist, but the titles are invisible to the host without a signature. Separately, .110, .123 and .171 report the SAME GAMEINDEX hash (9f4d3d9b), so an IP-keyed index can silently belong to another machine. Keying favorites_state and installed_games by hostname (FAV-8/N3) is the durable fix. This build only skips a box whose re-index failed this pass.
risks: The Team Arena writer is proven from the ioq3 source and the staged binary, and exercised against the captured .123 file, but it has not yet been seen on screen. TA's Join Server menu was reached on .195 (q3-195/45-ta-favorites.jpg), but UICLICK does not drive TA's mouse-only controls, so the Favorites check may need a person at the box.
The service runs scripts/gameindex/sync.py from the MAIN tree (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent). Restarting it before master is checked out there deploys nothing new.

The `players` column for q3/q2 rows now counts humans only (ping > 0). The Q3 internet favourites list can be shorter at quiet hours, and the per-engine player counts in status.json/the wall drop. This is intended per CLAUDE.md 'Bots are not players'. Bots with faked pings (the *A51* farms) still pass.
Incumbents are sticky by design: a listed internet server stays while it has at least one human. The file changes when a server empties or dies, not when a busier one appears.

A label change alone no longer triggers an upload. After a .132 outage, placeholder labels stay in comments and ini names until the server set changes (cosmetic; the games show live names once pinged).

Box files keep what the old writers put there, because nothing is ever deleted:
- the RTCW Main\autoexec.cfg server1 block and the Deus Ex favourites section (both inert);
- the phantom baseq3 folders in JediAcademy/SoF2/MOHAA, the q3bench block, and the .249 leftovers.
Cleanup is a later, separate write (FAV-8/FAV-12).
A box whose GAMESYNC STATUS says sizing/copying is skipped whole for that pass, so a hung or very long sync (e.g. .243) delays its favourites. This shows up as a BUSY line each pass.

Each pass DOWNLOADs the 692,748-byte servercache.dat from every box that has ioquake3 and a missionpack folder, to compare it. That is LAN traffic only and costs nothing on unchanged passes except the read.

Ownership of our Team Arena entries relies on a mark in netadr_t.ip6. That field is verified unread for NA_IP in this build. If a different ioquake3 is restaged, the md5-pin test fails, and the size check makes the writer refuse any other layout.
Win98 .243 gets one extra agent-internal command per pass (GAMESYNC STATUS). No process is spawned there.
hw_verification_plan:
DEPLOY
1. Commit the worktree changes: scripts/gameindex/{favorites,sync,db,masters}.py, scripts/gameindex/README.md, tests/python/test_gameindex_favorites.py and tests/python/test_patch_favourites.py. Also add the tests/README.md row.
2. Land them on master and fast-forward the MAIN tree (/home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent). The unit runs sync.py from there.
3. Run: systemctl --user restart retro-gameindex, then journalctl --user -u retro-gameindex -f for two passes (about 10 minutes).
There is no share publish and no agent release.

PASS 1: expect one-time writes per LCD box (.123 .145 .195 .240):
- 'ioquake3+quake3 q3 wrote 16 servers -> C:\Games\Quake3-TeamArena\baseq3\autoexec.cfg (…)'

PASS 2: every file line is 'unchanged: <path> (hash)', and status.json shows writes.wrote == 0 on a quiet fleet. If ok is false, the first error must be a real one.

READ-ONLY FILE CHECK on .240 (repeat on .123/.145/.195). DOWNLOAD C:\Documents and Settings\User\Application Data\Quake3\servercache.dat (on .195: C:\Users\admin\AppData\Roaming\Quake3\servercache.dat). Expect:
- 692,748 bytes;
- header (numglobal unchanged, 1, 692736);
- record at offset 671756: type 4, ip C0 A8 01 84, bytes 8-23 = 'retro-fleet-fav\0', port bytes 6D 3A, visible 1.
Also DOWNLOAD baseq3\autoexec.cfg: 'exec fleetres.cfg' is still present, and no ';' or '"' follows any '//' inside the managed block.

IN-GAME PROOF, fullscreen at 1920x1080:
1. Start 'Quake III - Team Arena' from its desktop shortcut (Play Team Arena.bat).
2. Go to Play/Multiplayer, then Join Server, then Source: Favorites. The TA menu bar is keyboard-navigable, but the Source control may need the mouse. .195's tester reached it (q3-195/45-ta-favorites.jpg); otherwise a person must do this once.
3. SCREENSHOT 0 works on XP. The frame must show the Favorites source listing NSC Retro Fleet Arena (Team Arena), 192.168.1.132:27962, answering with a ping.
4. Join it and screenshot in-game (clientinfo/scoreboard shows 192.168.1.132:27962).
5. Quit the game from its menu, not with taskkill. DOWNLOAD servercache.dat again: our entry is still there with its mark, and hostName is now the server's live name. The next pass must say 'unchanged'.

BUSY CHECK: while ioquake3 is running, the pass must log exactly one 'BUSY: C:\Games\Quake3-TeamArena\baseq3\autoexec.cfg: ioquake3.x86.exe is running …' and one 'missionpack q3cache BUSY: …servercache.dat: …'. There must be no 'wrote' line for either path in that pass.

MUST NOT CHANGE:

- TA's Source: Local still finds :27962.
- CS 1.6 favourites still list :27015/:27016; UT99, UT2004 and Unreal Gold favourites still list the fleet servers.
- Multiplayer joins on all of them still work.
- The 1080p resolution is untouched: fleetres.cfg is exec'd and r_mode -1 still applies.
- No new folders appear under C:\Games\JediAcademy, SoldierOfFortune2 or MOHAA, and nothing is written to .249.
- .243 (Win98) Quake2Win9x stays 'unchanged', and with QUAKE2.EXE running it now logs BUSY for that file.
review_notes:
SCOPE

Beyond the five asked-for items, I fixed these defects from the fav*-*.json audits. All are in scripts/gameindex and each has tests:
- FAV-2: DIRLIST answers [] for a missing folder, so emptiness is now proven one level up, and there is no MKDIR.
- FAV-1(b): a box whose GAMESYNC STATUS is sizing/copying is deferred.
- N2: when every local server is silent and the host does not hold its fleet address (ME), the pass reports ok:false.
- N3 (partial): a box whose re-index failed is not written.
- FAV-9/N4: files round-trip as latin-1.
- FAV-11: bots are not counted as players.
- FAV-5: seeds are not deduped by host, and RTT is timed to the first reply.
- F7: the vdf "address" key gets one tab, and a rewrite keeps the lastplayed stamp.
Each is small; the lead can drop any of them if it is too much.

Not done, deliberately:
- FAV-8: pruning stale favorites_state rows / keying by hostname.
- F9: *bak folders. The new no-parent check already skips System_226bak\System safely.
- Writers for HLDM appID 70, Far Cry and Tribes 2. Each needs a hardware check first; their reasons now say so.
- Filtering baseq3's internet list to gamename baseq3, which would drop the excessiveplus/freon mod servers. That is a one-word opt-in (strict_accepts=True on quake3/ioquake3), left for the lead to decide.

WHERE I DEPARTED FROM THE AUDITS
- The adversarial review said 'do not build a servercache.dat writer'. The task asked for one for Team Arena, and I built it with the safeguards the review wanted:
  - the layout is proven from the source AND the staged binary, and the binary is pinned by md5;
  - it is written only while no Q3 client runs, with PROCLIST asked again before the upload;
  - it is read back;
  - it is refused on any other layout;
  - only entries we marked are ever removed.
- For RTCW (WolfMP.exe's own layout) and JKA/SoF2 I did not build one: those layouts are unverified, and their reasons say so.
- wolfmp and deusex moved to UNWRITABLE. Two independent reviewers proved both writers were false successes. RTCW's MP UI has no 'server%d', and its servercache.dat read favourites=0 after sessions with server1 set. No DEUSEX.U class references UBrowserFavoritesFact.

NO PATCH TOOLING: favourites owns scripts/gameindex rather than provisioning/patches, so there is no apply.py and no --check/--build/--publish run. Nothing goes to the share (outputs/originals are empty). The sample merged servercache.dat for .123 is at ~/.retro-fleet/patch-out/favourites/servercache.dat.sample-123 (md5 852e1cf5e1208cb7f592e923c3d1ed44), built from the captured box file.

EVIDENCE (.claude/evidence-1080p/build-favourites/)
- servercache-layout-verification.txt: source and disassembly excerpts.
- halflife-won-protocol-45.txt.
- staged-autoexec-semicolons.txt: the library comments that execute as commands.
- offline-replay.txt.
- gameindex.diff: the full diff.
- pytest-run.txt.
- NOTES.txt.

Files modified in the worktree, uncommitted: scripts/gameindex/{favorites,sync,db,masters}.py, scripts/gameindex/README.md, tests/python/test_gameindex_favorites.py. New: tests/python/test_patch_favourites.py.

Interface kept: sync.unmanaged_modern_host (used by test_autodeploy) and the literal strings the no-clobber, modern-host and scan-cost tests pin. read_existing still returns a 3-tuple, with a new state 'no-parent'.

Push results are now one line per FILE, labelled with the joined keys (e.g. 'ioquake3+quake3'), and each note starts with the same prefix as before (wrote/unchanged/BUSY/skipped/FAILED). The wall's wrote/unchanged counts therefore count files, not titles.
